text:
maria.k: Heads-up — customer on Dedicated reported a sudden spike of 429s + duplicate billing after we merged the OpenAPI regen last night. They say Node + Go clients retried twice for the same idempotency token. repro below. anyone seen something similar? :alarm_clock:

tim.c: ugh. did they regenerate clients or are they using pinned versions?

maria.k: they upgraded the generated clients to latest. Python stayed on old pinned version, Node/Go regenerated. behavior only when using our client-side retry wrapper + `Idempotency-Key` header set by user.

olivia: can you paste the request/response traces (with headers redacted)?

maria.k: sure. trimmed:```
POST /v1/generate
Idempotency-Key: abc-123
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
User-Agent: redwood-node/2.1.0

> 200 OK x-request-id: req_789 latency_ms: 320
> 409 Conflict x-error: already-processed

Then client retried and we saw:
> 201 Created x-request-id: req_790
> 201 Created x-request-id: req_791
```

chen: interesting — regen changed the ordering of optional `retry` query vs `timeout` parameter in the OpenAPI schema? that can shift how the generated client serializes header vs query for some languages. if Idempotency-Key ended up in query for Go/TS it would bypass our idempotency check.

tim.c: iirc there was a patch where `x-idempotency-header` got renamed to `idempotency_key` in the schema but kept `header` style in docs. might be a drift between codegen templates and schema.

olivia: can we reproduce locally with the same generated client version? steps?

maria.k: repro steps i used: 1) regen node client from branch `openapi/2026-03-param-order` 2) run tiny script that sets Idempotency-Key and calls generate concurrently 3) inspect outgoing wire with mitmproxy

ci-bot: build #4521 for openapi/2026-03-param-order finished (codegen: node-go-python) — artifacts at s3://ci-artifacts/4521

chen: copying the minimal node script:
```js
const client = require('./generated');
async function f(){
  const key = 'test-'+Date.now();
  await Promise.all([client.generate({idempotencyKey: key}), client.generate({idempotencyKey: key})]);
}
f();
```

maria.k: that reproduces it locally. mitm shows first request puts `idempotency_key` in querystring not header for node/go codegen. python client still uses header.

tim.c: this would explain double billing (server treated them as distinct requests) and also the 429 burst (retry loop). we need a quick mitigation — can we patch runtime to prefer Idempotency-Key header on server-side if present in either place? fallback logic?

olivia: server-side fallback risky for compat. alternative: patch the codegen templates to force `style: header` and cut a hotfix regen for Node+Go, publish a patch client release and ask customers to upgrade. canary rollout on Dedicated first.

maria.k: agreed. i'm drafting customer note. support-bot: I've opened ticket #CS-3412 and attached repro logs. customer is sensitive (billing).

chen: I started a bisect of the openapi commits — looks like `openapi.yaml` change in commit d4a9b2 swapped parameter `in:` from header -> query for `idempotency_key` during an automated schema normalize step. will open PR to revert + add unit test.

tim.c: quick stopgap — can we add a compatibility check in our SDK runtime that, if `Idempotency-Key` not found in headers but `idempotency_key` present in query, we treat them as same token for 48h? patch server: redwood-inference/ingress checks.

olivia: ok to implement a 48h compatibility layer with telemetry flag. we should also run a job that scans recent requests for `idempotency_key` in query to estimate exposure.

maria.k: plan for release: (1) server compatibility patch deployed to Dedicated regions now (2) PR to revert openapi param change and regen clients (node/go) (3) patch releases for affected client versions + customer advisory (4) billing remediation manual review for CS ticket.

tim.c: i'll take the revert PR + regen for node/go. chen do you want to own the server fallback?

chen: yep i'll open a small patch, add a feature-flagged fallback and metric `compat.idempotency_in_query`

olivia: devex action items: update codegen tests to include explicit `in: header` checks and add a CI gate that prevents OpenAPI normalizer from converting header params to query unless schema explicitly states it. i'll file a follow-up.

maria.k: thanks all. keeping customer in the loop. will post updates here and on #support. :white_check_mark:
